statement: PRIOR-ART CORRECTION (protect against claiming known results as new). CRUCIAL distinction: Boralevi et al. 2025's equidimensionality result is for the RECTANGULAR variety P_{4,5} (4x5 matrix, 20 vars, all 4x4 permanents=0). Our non-equidimensionality result is for the SQUARE critical locus Sigma(perm_5)=Crit(perm_5) (5x5 matrix, 25 vars, all 4x4 sub-permanents=0) - a DIFFERENT variety (different ambient dim 25 vs 20, different equations 25 vs 5). Our block component V_{2,3}=diag(B_{2x2},C_{3x3}) is square-specific and not in their rectangular Table 1. KNOWN components reused: the 15-dim vanishing-row linear spaces (Boralevi Prop 3.8; Xie) and the W_{1,4} vanishing-row+col+complementary-perm type (Blaeser et al 2017). STATUS OF NOVELTY: the SQUARE non-equidimensionality and the explicit 11-dim block component V_{2,3} were NOT found in the surveyed literature (Boralevi 2025 is rectangular-equidimensional; Xie 2026 global-dim-only; Blaeser 2017 / Kirkup 2005 do not address it), but a FULL novelty determination requires confirming no prior treatment of the SQUARE critical locus's component/equidimensionality structure. We do NOT claim the result as definitively new; the VERIFIED FACT (Sigma(perm_5) non-equidimensional, dim 11 and 15, three-way exact) stands regardless of novelty.

statement: FruitStack-coordinated structural finding (2 PlumMe models + adversarial researcher). The models suggested the Young-flattening/catalecticant lever (Landsberg-Manivel) to avoid weight-space enumeration. (1) Joint pivot over F_2: exists t with a_i t + b_i = 0 for all i <=> (1+a_i)b_i = 0 and a_i b_j + a_j b_i = 0 (all i,j); one step raises degree to <= 3 from quadratic. Over F_3 with Boolean t the formula is false (8 counterexamples for m=2, e.g. a=(0,1), b=(0,2)). (2) Any system in visible variables only describing d = x_1...x_n needs an equation of degree >= n (restrict d=0; multilinear representation unique, indicator of 1^n is prod x_i); d - prod x_i attains n; holds over every field. (3) Positive exact-one AND gate E(t,u,~a), E(t,v,~b), E(u,v,s) forces t = ab (s = XNOR, third clause forces uv=0); complements via E(x,~x,z); zero without repeated literals: E(x,y,z), E(x,y,w), E(z,w,r) forces z=w=0. Chain checked n<=6: projection = graph of AND_n, aux unique. O(n) clauses, bounded treewidth (path decomposition per gate plus z; width not computed). Consequence: degree after elimination is unbounded already at bounded treewidth, while the factored (aux/extension) form has width 2. The fitting measure is width/rank of the factored representation, for which 17405 (CLAIMED) gives 2^p for P_B; degree lower bounds (BGIP 2001) are for PC without extension variables. Not in proofbook before (closest: ACC0-L3 class D, row 4864, NAND gadget over GF(3)). No obligation closed, no runtime bound.

statement: SCOPE CHECK of the law cov = rank3 + 1 on GF(3)-blind positive 1-in-3 families (director 2026-11-21, owner request): FALSE in general. Exact counterexamples: core F0 = {012,013,045,145,234,235} is blind with cov 6, rank3 5 (difference 1), but F0 + {678} is blind with cov 9, rank3 6 (difference 3) and F0 + a disjoint shifted copy is blind with cov 12, rank3 10 (difference 2) - for variable-disjoint families cov and rank add, consistency and unsatisfiability are kept. This refutes the general claims claim:adb072e397b9 and claim:b74d679e26ba as stated. PROVED (elementary): a minimally blind family (blind, no proper subfamily blind) is connected; and minimality needs only the subfamilies with one clause removed. NOT proved: minimally blind => cov = rank3 + 1. Finite evidence (exhaustive, all families on <= 6 variables with m <= 8 clauses): all 900 minimally blind families have m = 5 and cov - rank3 = 1, no counterexample. The dataset laws on n = 7, m = 6 and n = 8 hold there by the size constraint (two disjoint blind cores need more variables), which explains the observation without supporting the general law. Owner decision: no further four-agent campaign on this law until the minimal-core version is proved or refuted.

structure.statement: OPS Theorem 1.4 is the general-circuit magnification statement for Gap-MCSP thresholds [2^{beta n}/(c n), 2^{beta n}], with exists epsilon followed by every sufficiently small beta. OPS Theorem 1.5 is a separate U2-formula lower bound for thresholds [n^d, 2^{(alpha/2-o(1))n}]. Theorem 1.5 alone does not establish Theorem 1.4's premise because both the model and thresholds differ; OPS explicitly notes that Theorem 1.4's argument fails for formulas.

structure.text: Repair of the residual factorization claim: the successor residual is a well-defined function of the current reachable residual and next bit, T_t(R,b)={z:bz∈R}. This follows directly from exact deterministic continuation behavior. Circuit implementations of π_t(q) and π_{t+1}(q) on machine-state inputs do not imply a circuit implementation on residual encodings; no cost bound is established.

statement: MECHANISM mech:weighted-cnf-inclusion-exclusion-cut-matrix: The cut matrix M(x,y)=g(x,y)·1[F(x,y)] has rank at most 2^m r.

bingo.correctness: Inclusion-exclusion expands 1[F] over at most 2^m clause subsets. Each nonzero indicator that selected clauses are falsified factors across X|Y and has rank one. Hadamard multiplication by the cut matrix of g gives rank at most r per term; rank subadditivity yields the bound.
bingo.effect: The cut matrix M(x,y)=g(x,y)·1[F(x,y)] has rank at most 2^m r.
bingo.interfaces: Input: F, cut X|Y, and g. Output: a structural rank bound for the weighted satisfying-assignment matrix.
bingo.limitations: The expansion has up to 2^m terms. This gives no efficient counting algorithm or P versus NP consequence. T52 elimination and Koopman observation-space evaluation are not used, and their hypotheses are not established for general CNFs.
bingo.name: Weighted CNF inclusion-exclusion cut matrix
bingo.preconditions: Finite CNF F with m clauses; any partition X|Y of Boolean variables; field-valued weight function g whose X|Y cut matrix has rank r.

bingo.representations: Field-valued cut matrices indexed by assignments to X and Y; clause-subset inclusion-exclusion terms.

statement: TARGET READING (owner 2026-11-19): the original TARGET entry states P != NP; the research objective is to DECIDE P vs NP. Both directions are pursued with equal standing. P = NP needs one algorithm for positive 1-in-3-SAT (NP-complete), correct on every formula with polynomial size/construction/decision; P != NP needs a theorem excluding every polynomial algorithm. Findings about one method (GF(3) blindness, Nullstellensatz degree, failed relaxations) are limits of that method and count for neither direction by themselves.

statement: BEYOND PC (owner deep research 2026-11-19, director checks): (1) IPS TRANSFER SCHEMA: in GF(2)[x,y] (no multilinearisation) the substitution y -> 1+a+b maps L_edge to 0, q_edge to ab + (a^2+a) + (b^2+b), y^2+y to (a^2+a)+(b^2+b) (sympy-checked); vertex axioms map to colouring axioms. Substituting a 3-term affine form into an ARITHMETIC CIRCUIT costs only additive size, so a size-s circuit-coefficient IPS refutation of F(G) gives a size-O(s+|G|) IPS refutation of the 3-colouring axioms of G (formal size statement still to be fixed). Unlike roABP-IPS (order-sensitive), general IPS has no width obstacle here. (2) Grochow-Pitassi 2014: any superpolynomial IPS lower bound implies VP != VNP - so an IPS lower bound for F(G) is at least as hard as VP != VNP; the transfer shows F(G) is no easier than 3-colouring, it does not provide the bound. (3) Hardness magnification (Oliveira-Pich-Santhanam): slightly superlinear bounds for Gap-MCSP would give NP not in P/poly; director note: magnification is limited by the LOCALITY BARRIER (Chen-Hirahara-Oliveira-Pich-Rajgopal-Santhanam 2020) - known lower-bound techniques extend to oracle-augmented circuits and cannot supply the needed bounds. No direct link from our 1-in-3 results. (4) Quantifier gap stays explicit: hard instances for a proof system say nothing about every circuit computing SAT_N. (5) Mishra-Santhanam 4n - O(log n): still only verified by the director as a STOC 2027 submission claim.

statement: ORACLE ELIMINATION COUNT DOES NOT BEAR ON ALGEBRIZATION; PI CORRECTION (owner 2026-11-27; PI check; CLAIMED, Claude family; AW from memory). Owner's (a) no p(m)-bit oracle-free graph represents every A:{0,1}^m->{0,1} (2^{2^m} > 2^{p(m)+1}) and (b) a query compiler needs B >= 2^m answer bits: both correct, and both are the Shannon counting argument. They hold for every oracle, algebraic or not, so they cannot separate algebrizing from non-algebrizing proofs. No relativized or algebrized proof eliminates the oracle; the standard relativized form keeps oracle gates as external oracle constraints (relativized Cook-Levin), and the algebrization test asks whether each step stays valid with Ã-constraints on the C side and A on the D side. Explicit local decomposition (local checkability, Arora-Impagliazzo-Vazirani) is exactly what arithmetization uses, and AW show arithmetization-based results such as IP=PSPACE algebrize. PI correction to the 2026-11-27 chat proposal: 'all tools algebrize => no combination proves P!=NP' is too strong. AW algebrization is asymmetric (Ã vs A) and not closed under composition of inclusions, so a tool-level check is necessary but not sufficient. The whole proof must be tested. No obligation closed.

structure.question: Q-34b02a6004
structure.text: SOURCE CHECK row G (Stage A, lane T-B). Source read: arXiv 2312.08163v1, Pich-Santhanam, 'Towards P != NP from Extended Frege lower bounds' (the longer version of ECCC TR23-199; the ECCC PDF was NOT read). Read via web_read at offset 0 and 4500. Theorem 1 (extraction, verbatim wording as far as the text goes): let k>=1 be constant. (1) If there is a p-time f such that for each big n, wk_n(f) is a tautology, and EF + wk(f) is not p-bounded, then SAT_n is not in Circuit[n^{eps k}] for infinitely many n. (2) If there is a p-time f with S12 proving W^k_{n0}(f) for some n0, and EF is not p-bounded, the same conclusion holds. eps>0 is universal. Corollary 1 (partial extraction): if for every k there is a p-time f_k with wk_n(f_k) tautologies for big n, and EF + wk(f_k) is not p-bounded for each k, then NP is not in SIZE[n^l] for every l, i.e. SAT is not in P/poly. Scope and status: row G's conclusion (SAT not in P/poly) needs (i) witnessing functions f_k for EVERY k and (ii) the superpolynomial proof-size lower bound for EF + wk(f_k). The paper says it does NOT know an unconditional witnessing function (it is the step it cannot yet discharge). Row G is therefore VERIFIED AS A CONDITIONAL STATEMENT; both (i) and (ii) remain open. The abstract's separate P != NP route (conditions I-II, S12 witnessing) is not the row-G route and is not checked here.

statement: Dispute K11-D5, resolved on the H2 point by source. MMW19 (STOC 2019) Thm 1.4 bullet 3 (primary PDF, offset 13500; proof at offset 53500, sha256 7077714b...): for s(n) >= n and A in PH, if search-MCSP^A[s(n)] on N=2^n inputs has no circuits of size N*poly(s(n)) and depth poly(s(n)), then NP not in P/poly. The proof is a contrapositive: NP in P/poly collapses PH to P/poly, and the Lemma 3.1 construction is uniform in n, so it yields small circuits at every input length. CONSEQUENCES: (1) the NP-to-small-MCSP conversion (the former H2) is inside the theorem, not an extra premise; (2) the quantifier is therefore 'infinitely many n' (inferred from the proof structure, not verbatim text); (3) with A empty and s(n)=n^c, a general-circuit lower bound N*(log N)^k for every fixed k, infinitely often, for decision MCSP[m^c] gives the search hypothesis, because a decision circuit of size N*poly(s) and depth poly(s) yields a search circuit of the same size and depth (flag bit; the flag-bit cost itself is not checked here). OPEN: H1 itself (a general-circuit decision lower bound for MCSP[m^c] at N*(log N)^k, infinitely often) is unproved and is the only remaining obligation; see Q-10bbdfaf2a and Q-f1e058b72f. This is a magnification connection, not a LOWER_BOUND record, and not a lemma.

statement: Owner's factorized-sparsity operator U_R = B V_R B (B = H^{otimes m}, V_R a reversible Toffoli-type verifier), PI check 2026-11-27. CLAIMED. Verified: <x,0,1|U_R|x,0,0> = N(x)/2^m (the Hadamard row 0 is all +, and V_R preserves z), so exists z <=> entry != 0; factors have <=2 nonzeros per row/column, condition number 1, poly many. Known mechanism (sum over paths / strong simulation; owner claims no novelty). Classification (from memory, unverified): the nonzero test of a single entry is NP-complete for interference-free (nonnegative) products such as B V B, and NQP = coC=P-complete for general H+Toffoli products with signs. Hence the operation E(S_1..S_k) restricted to the owner's family is an NP-complete problem: a law forbidding its efficient evaluation is equivalent to P != NP (equivalent reformulation, not a route). The formalism relativizes (an oracle enters as a permutation factor), so properties of the factor structure alone algebrize/relativize (T49 Lemma 4); a white-box law about poly-size deciders is again needed. Matrix entry = counting (#P), nonzero = existence: this is the operator form of T53 E1/E2. No contradiction.

statement: The universal form of the law sat = cons3 over all positive 1-in-3 formulas is equivalent to P = NP: cons3 is decidable in polynomial time by Gaussian elimination over GF(3), and 1-in-3-SAT is NP-complete. So the exact-law question on this family is a restatement of P vs NP, not a route around it. Finite data can only locate the boundary of the law; the boundary currently sits in the random n=10-12 and targeted rank-7-9 families.

Verbatim quantifiers: (Thm 1.2) for s(n) >= n time-constructible and any oracle A, one-pass streaming for search-MCSP^A[s] on 2^n-bit inputs runs in 2^n * O~(s) time, O~(s^2) worst-case update time, O~(s) space, using a Sigma3SAT^A oracle with queries of length O~(s). Algorithm 1 consumes t = 100 s log s bits per block; its update-time analysis (Sec. 4 proof) gives O~(t^2) per block, consistent with Thm 1.2. (Thm 1.3) If there is A in PH such that search-MCSP^A[s] has no poly(s)-space streaming algorithm with poly(s) update time, then P != NP. Proof (Sec. 5, read at offset 49500): contrapositive; under P = NP, PH collapses, Sigma3SAT^A is in P for every A in PH, each Circuit-Min-Merge query of length O(s log s) is replaced by a poly(s)-time computation, giving poly(s) update time. (Thm 1.4 and 1.5 read at offsets 54000 and 58500; statements as in the bridge map.) Scope: this is a source verification of statements and proof structure only. It does not verify the 2^n*s total-time accounting beyond cm-b098520d49db4fa4, and it does not establish any lower bound. The lower bound needed for P != NP is an update-time lower bound (space and communication alone cannot reach it, per the owner's note), and none is proved here.

statement: FOUR-DIMENSION PROFILE (owner 2026-11-19, replaces the 'common axis'): every representation sigma(F) of a formula is judged on (1) EXACTNESS - is the decision information present; (2) SIZE - worst-case size; (3) CONSTRUCTION - cost to build it from F (and to update it clause by clause); (4) EVALUATION - cost to extract SAT from it. Two different failure kinds: INFORMATION LOSS (a summary like [V_F != empty] maps a satisfiable and a GF(3)-blind UNSAT formula to the same value - 1,350 blind sets at n=6) versus HARD EXTRACTION: the full affine GF(3) solution space V_F = {x in F_3^n : A x = 1} is built by Gaussian elimination in polynomial time and is EXACT, since a clause sum over {0,1} is in 0..3 and only 1 is 1 mod 3, so V_F intersect {0,1}^n = the Boolean solutions; deciding whether an affine subspace of F_3^n contains a 0/1 point is therefore NP-complete. Indistinguishability pairs can never refute an exact representation; for those the open question is the evaluation cost. P = NP needs all four dimensions polynomial for every F; a limit of one representation or one evaluation method is not P != NP. Measured Nullstellensatz degrees on finite instances (local degree 4 at k=17) are data, not an asymptotic growth claim; n^O(d) is an upper bound for degree-d search only.

statement: VERIFIED ALGEBRAIC TRANSFER, steps 4-6 (owner contract 2026-11-27; PI reading of both papers; CLAIMED, Claude family). EXTERNAL INPUTS, UNVERIFIED, kept separate from Proofbook results: OpenAI 'VP and VNP are different' (openai/math 3344da5, Lean OAI.Computability.VPVNP.Standalone.vp_ne_vnp) and Anthropic 'VP != VNP over every field' (anthropics/formal-math 11b6c7e, vp-vnp, Lean Solution.mainTheorem etc.). Kernel build, #print axioms and Comparator are running in a bwrap sandbox; results follow in a separate row. STEP 4, mechanism. Both proofs trade tensor rigidity against diagonalization. Anthropic: Thm 2.2 (thm_alt) gives a flat or a contracting case. Flat case: lem_balanced splits the polynomial at every gate, so the output coefficient tensor is a sum of terms of rank <= L across balanced sets; Euclidean prices force log L >= l k^{3/2}/16 for f_{k,l}. Contracting case: thm_cut, with no circuit, cuts every weighted nondeterministic computation into short pieces; lem_lowdeg turns a circuit of size v^a into an accelerator, a program whose circuit constants act only as multiplicative named weights and whose runs take v^{H-16} < v^H steps; lem_postpone and prop_next amplify; thm_noacc gives V = 1 + V, impossible. OpenAI: Euclidean tensor pricing (exists_balanced_cutFactors, see 17563) plus replay diagonalization against the counting family f_n, whose c_x counts accepting paths of a universal machine. In both proofs the circuit enters only at the C-steps (formal multilinear block part or formal low-degree part); the hard families enter only through clause sums. STEP 5, translation. By 17584 over the semiring F[Y] with weights set to variables, every clause sum is a p-projection of U_G for a polynomial-size pinned graph G: boolean vertices carry the bits, AND gadgets give indicator vertices for local assignments, and their colour-1 variables are replaced by the local weights. f_{k,l}, Phi and f_n are clause sums, so each is a projection of a U_G family. This is a corollary of 17584 and not new; Valiant/Buergisser parsimonious completeness is standard (from memory). Consequence, conditional on the external results: the U_G families are not in VP. That is a consequence, not a premise. STEP 6, P = NP against intermediate theorems; result negative and exact. (a) C-steps. A polynomial-time SAT algorithm yields Boolean circuits, that is F2-circuits for some g = f + sum_i (x_i^2 - x_i) h_i. lem_balanced and lem_lowdeg read the multilinear block part and the low-degree part of the formal output, and for such g these are unrelated to f. Counterexamples: Anthropic Sec. 2.5, where (x11^2 - x11) x21...xk1 vanishes on {0,1} but has nonzero block-linear part; 17571, IP_n with a linear-size circuit and full cut rank. So the hypotheses of the C-steps are not met. (b) Diagonal step. thm_noacc refutes accelerators. A uniform algorithm from P = NP, or even from P^#P = P, is an accelerator only if it computes the weighted sum of tau-plain instances, size v^{H-32}, in v^{H-16} steps. Collapse simulations raise the time exponent by the factor c of the assumed algorithm and never lower it below the plain-run bound, so no accelerator arises. A nonuniform Boolean circuit branches on its advice; that is excluded by the model, because names may only be multiplied in (Anthropic 2.5: 'no way to run it faster than gate by gate'). Hence no intermediate theorem of either proof is contradicted by P = NP along these derivations. The exact obstruction: formal polynomial structure (C-steps) and exponent-lowering speedup in the weighted-sum model (diagonal step). No new lower-bound premise and no conditional chain; no obligation closed.

statement: SOURCE CHECK, row A, A.3 (Oliveira-Pich-Santhanam, Hardness Magnification Near State-of-the-Art Lower Bounds, Oxford preprint hm.pdf, read at offset 88500). (a) A.3 is a SKETCH ('we sketch the proof of Theorem 5'), not a full proof. (b) Its lower bound is against U2-FORMULAS, not general circuits; item (1) of the Theorem requires Gap-MCSP[2^{beta n}/cn, 2^{beta n}] not in Circuit[N^{1+eps}]. A formula bound does not transfer to a circuit bound, so A.3 does NOT supply the item (1) hypothesis. (c) The range is Gap-MCSP[n^d, 2^{(alpha/2 - o(1))n}] (polynomial threshold, parameter alpha), not the 2^{beta n}/cn range of item (1). Quantifier reading of item (1) still needs primary-source verification (Zesty2 HTTP 422, CORE CAPTCHA). Scope: source check, not a proof step.

(1) The LP relaxation is NEVER infeasible: x = 1/3 everywhere satisfies every clause (D-016h), so pure linear arithmetic over [0,1] refutes no positive 1-in-3 formula. (2) Depth-1 Chvatal-Gomory from A x = 1 alone refutes exactly the integer-infeasible formulas (D-023, integer Farkas / Hermite normal form). (3) Of the 1,350 GF(3)-blind sets at n=6 only 30 are integer-infeasible (R0100/R0101). So the cheap PB steps catch 30 of 1,350; the other 1,320 need the bounds 0 <= x <= 1 combined with deeper cuts or conflict learning - that is where the PB information difference sits.

statement: BRIDGE STATUS (owner 2026-11-19, literature-checked): (1) A computation trace is NOT an UNSAT proof by itself (an always-UNSAT program has short checkable traces); it becomes one only together with a proof of the algorithm s correctness. Precise known form: if the correctness of a poly-time algorithm A is provable in the bounded arithmetic PV (S^1_2), then A s UNSAT answers translate into polynomial-size Extended Frege proofs (Cook 1975; Krajicek-Pudlak). An EF lower bound would therefore exclude all poly-time algorithms with PV-provable correctness, not all algorithms. (2) Cook-Reckhow: NP = coNP iff some propositional proof system is polynomially bounded; superpolynomial lower bounds for EVERY proof system give NP != coNP (hence P != NP); a lower bound for one system (PC, EF) does not, since existence of a p-optimal proof system is open. (3) Alekseev, A lower bound for polynomial calculus with extension rule (CCC 2021 version; owner cites 2026 journal version): exponential BIT-SIZE lower bound over Q for the Binary Value Principle 1 + x1 + 2x2 + ... + 2^(n-1)xn = 0 in PC with extension variables (and radical-type rules) - bit-level/coefficient size as the measured resource, not a CNF and not over GF(2). For ALG-BIT-001 (no new assignment): report the coefficient BIT SIZE of certificates alongside degree when working over Q/Z (e.g. integer-sum refutations of blind cores, which relate to the CG certificates).

structure.statement: BRIDGE STATUS (owner 2026-11-19, literature-checked): (1) A computation trace is NOT an UNSAT proof by itself (an always-UNSAT program has short checkable traces); it becomes one only together with a proof of the algorithm s correctness. Precise known form: if the correctness of a poly-time algorithm A is provable in the bounded arithmetic PV (S^1_2), then A s UNSAT answers translate into polynomial-size Extended Frege proofs (Cook 1975; Krajicek-Pudlak). An EF lower bound would therefore exclude all poly-time algorithms with PV-provable correctness, not all algorithms. (2) Cook-Reckhow: NP = coNP iff some propositional proof system is polynomially bounded; superpolynomial lower bounds for EVERY proof system give NP != coNP (hence P != NP); a lower bound for one system (PC, EF) does not, since existence of a p-optimal proof system is open.
